finding.claim: The /checkout route computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set arbitrary prices, or negative or zero quantities, to pay less than the real price or get a negative total (a refund or credit). The server never looks up the price and never validates qty.

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty taken directly from the request body, with no catalog lookup and no bounds check
total is passed to the payment charge call for the user
the response confirms the attacker-chosen amount was charged

finding.guards_checked: No catalog price lookup, no qty integer or positive validation, no minimum total check, and no auth middleware visible in this file. The safer /checkout-v2 route in the same file uses req.catalog.price() and clamps qty, which shows the intended control is missing from /checkout. /checkout is still routable.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or qty validation, cart.js:6 charges that total and cart.js:7 returns it, and the only controls (catalog.price and the qty clamp) are in /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14, so /checkout has none. The attacker only needs to be a logged-in user, since req.user.id is used, and no other file in the directory adds middleware.
